acceptance_tests.evidence: 409 returns a RESULT {status:409, conflict:true, created:false, current_revision:3} and does not throw; a 500 throws ApiError{status:500, code:'server_error', conflict:false, outcome:'rejected'}. A dedicated test asserts both together: conflict.status !== serverErr.status and conflict.created === false, so no caller can render 'Saved'.

An HTML 502 produces an ApiError with code 'upstream_unavailable' whose message matches /502/ and does NOT match /JSON|Unexpected token|is not valid/i, and is not a SyntaxError. A separate test spies on the Response: text() called exactly once, json() never called — the body is read once. An empty 400 body also yields a typed error.

An AbortError becomes {status:null, code:'aborted', outcome:'rejected'} with a message that never matches /500|server/i. listImages and getImage are each called with a controller and the stubbed fetch is asserted to receive that exact signal on both calls. isRetryable(aborted) is false.

A TypeError from fetch on submitReview yields {code:'network', status:null, outcome:'unknown', mayHaveCommitted:true}. An AbortError on the same mutation yields {code:'aborted', outcome:'rejected', mayHaveCommitted:false}. Two further tests assert the stubbed fetch was called EXACTLY ONCE for both a network failure and a 500 — mutations are never auto-retried.

A 401 on /api/v1/images yields code 'auth_required' after exactly one call; calls[0].url === '/api/v1/images' and startsWith('/v1/') is false, so the URL is never rewritten to the unauthenticated local G6 path. isRetryable is false for both 401 and 403. getReview under 401 also produces exactly one call.

limitations: A FOURTH defect was found in this task's own code during the completion check and fixed: submitReview hardcoded `status: 200`, but the backend answers 201 for a newly created event and 200 for an idempotent replay. The previous implementation reported the real status, so this was a regression that would have broken R006's retry reconciliation later. Fixed by adding request<T>() which returns {status, data, request_id}, with fetchJson layered on top; submitReview now reports result.status. Locked by three new tests (201 created, 200 replay, and request() exposing both).

My earlier claim that the browser E2E suite did not need re-running because 'no product code changed' was WRONG for a frontend task: api.ts IS product code and e2e exercises every review action through the rewritten client. Re-run during the completion check: 17/17 passed, exit 0.

THREE defects in this task's own code were found and fixed, all disclosed rather than smoothed over: (1) apiErrors.ts imported ITSELF via `export { ApiError as ApiErrorClass } from "./apiErrors"` — vitest tolerated it, node refused it with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, found only by running the sweep outside the test harness; (2) api.ts ended with a bare CR (248 CR vs 247 LF), making the task's own `git diff --check` exit 2 and flag every line as trailing whitespace; (3) `isRetryable` was imported into api.ts but only re-exported, caught by the TypeScript build gate as TS6133. All three were fixed at the cause; no lint suppression and no weakened assertion.

Five assertions in my own first draft of the acceptance test were wrong and were corrected, not weakened: an untyped `expect(conflictErr).toBeUndefined()`; a `.json()` spy that could never fire because the client reads via `text()`; a `not.toContain('/v1/images')` check that a valid '/api/v1/images' URL necessarily fails; and two calls to `api.getReview`/`api.exportUrl` when those are named exports, not members of the `api` namespace object.
The TypeScript build gate caught 8 union-type errors caused by `.catch(e => e as ApiError)` widening the result; fixed with a properly typed `rejection()` helper rather than by loosening types.
The client is exercised only against a stubbed fetch. No live-browser or live-backend verification of the new error paths was performed.
No component consumes outcome/mayHaveCommitted/api.lastRequestId yet; the capability exists and is tested but is not yet visible in the UI.

The enterprise frontend's own api.ts still throws plain Error with stringified JSON. It was read as a pattern reference only and deliberately NOT migrated — that is E001-E003 territory and outside this task's 3-file surface.
Real Grad-CAM, the original G4 bundle, WSI, and any cloud resource remain unexercised. No backend, database, or model code was touched by this task.

boundary_observations: no rows / one row: not applicable to a transport layer; the empty and single-response paths are covered by decodeBody's null, empty-string, scalar, array and malformed inputs
duplicate input/retry: a replayed read is bounded and cancellable; a replayed WRITE is never issued automatically — asserted by call-count, not by flag
missing or malformed values: a non-JSON, HTML, empty, or scalar error body all yield a typed ApiError with a readable message instead of a parse exception
unavailable artifact: 502/503/504 map to 'upstream_unavailable' with a distinct code from a plain 500
unauthorized object: 401/403 are classified and are never retryable, so the client cannot silently fall back to the unauthenticated local /v1/ endpoint
changed project/model/session: the client holds no project or model state; every request is built from the caller's path with no global authority that could leak scope
stale response: a deferred-promise test resolves B before A and asserts the order; api.lastRequestId() gives each request a monotonic identity
canceled request: AbortError is classified as 'aborted', never as a server failure, and is not retryable
partial failure: a network drop during a write reports outcome 'unknown' with mayHaveCommitted true — the client never promises the write did not land
redaction: safeDetail removes tokens, signed-URL signatures, absolute server paths and stack traces while preserving the safe message; a cyclic object terminates instead of recursing
